stem: Amoxicillin is used to treat which of the following pairs of infections?

options.label: A
options.text: Bacterial pneumonia and urinary tract infections
options.misconception: None — amoxicillin treats certain bacterial infections, including pneumonia and urinary tract infections.
options.explanation: MedlinePlus lists amoxicillin for certain infections caused by bacteria, such as pneumonia, skin infections and urinary tract infections.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Assumes a drug that treats typical bacterial pneumonia also covers atypical organisms.
options.explanation: Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall and Legionella lives inside cells, so atypical pneumonia needs a macrolide, doxycycline or fluoroquinolone, not amoxicillin.

options.label: C
options.text: Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus infections
options.misconception: Believes antibiotics help viral respiratory infections, a common driver of inappropriate prescribing.
options.explanation: Influenza and RSV are viruses with no peptidoglycan, so amoxicillin has no effect on them; influenza is treated with antivirals such as oseltamivir.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Assumes a penicillin like amoxicillin acts on protozoa, which lack the peptidoglycan it targets.
options.explanation: Giardia and Plasmodium are protozoa, which lack peptidoglycan, so a penicillin such as amoxicillin has no activity against them.

options.label: E
options.text: MRSA bacteremia and MRSA skin abscesses
options.misconception: Assumes any staphylococcal infection responds to a penicillin, overlooking methicillin resistance.
options.explanation: MRSA carries an altered penicillin-binding protein (PBP2a) that resists beta-lactams such as amoxicillin; vancomycin or another anti-MRSA drug is needed.

context: Learning objective: Amoxicillin treats certain bacterial infections, such as pneumonia, skin infections and urinary tract infections.
